subject: SLA availability quantum & maintenance notification protocol - redlines from Auriga
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lang <peter.lang@auriga.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Jul 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: SLA availability quantum & maintenance notification protocol - initial redlines

Hi Peter,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is our annotated MSA + Order Form with the initial support/SLA redlines we discussed (see Auriga_SLA_Redlines_20280702.pdf). High level items we flagged:

- Availability banding: we proposed 99.95% and 99.99% tiers with tiered credits. Please confirm if Auriga needs a minimum of 99.995% for any critical endpoints.
- Service credit calculation: we used a monthly measurement window and sliding credit formula tied to uptime buckets (details in sla-credit-matrix-proposal.xlsx).
- P1 response / on-call: targeted 1 hour acknowledge, 4 hour initial mitigation plan.
- Maintenance windows: maintenance exclusions limited to quarterly planned windows with 72-hour advance notice; emergency patch windows allowed with post-facto notice and limited credit carveouts.

Request: please share Auriga's redline PDF by EOD Wednesday so we can route to legal and ops. If Auriga wants narrower maintenance notification (48h) or different credit math, flag in your redlines.

Attachments: Auriga_SLA_Redlines_20280702.pdf (redline), sla-credit-matrix-proposal.xlsx (model)

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Peter Lang <peter.lang@auriga.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@auriga.com, Auriga Legal <legal@auriga.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA availability quantum & maintenance notification protocol - initial redlines

Laura —

Thanks for the note and redlines. We reviewed with procurement and legal. High-level Auriga asks (attached is our annotated response):

1) Availability target: Auriga cannot agree to 99.95% for our primary inference endpoint. We need a commitment to 99.99% monthly for that endpoint.
2) Credits: we prefer a flat per-minute credit beyond threshold rather than a sliding monthly bucket. Suggestion in our doc.
3) Maintenance notice: 48-hour advance notice for any planned maintenance that may affect that endpoint. Quarterly schedule is OK, but need shorter notification.
4) Regional failover: require a documented runbook and testing cadence in the Order Form.

We marked these in the attached PDF. We're open to trade-offs: if Redwood can accept 99.99% for primary endpoints, Auriga is willing to accept a slightly higher credit cap per month.

Att: Auriga_SLA_Response_20280703.pdf

Peter Lang
VP Procurement, Auriga Health
peter.lang@auriga.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lang <peter.lang@auriga.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SLA availability quantum & maintenance notification protocol - tradeoffs & internal ask

Peter — thanks for the clear asks and for calling out the runbook requirement. Quick operational posture from our side before legal dives in:

- 99.99% for a primary inference endpoint is materially tighter than our standard Order Form profile. We can explore it for a single production endpoint if we adjust the credit cap and agree on clear traffic shaping fallbacks.
- Flat per-minute credits: ops prefers bucketed monthly buckets (to avoid extreme single-minute volatility) but we can map to a per-minute-equivalent calculation in the Order Form if legal signs off.
- 48-hour maintenance notice: operationally tighter but feasible for scheduled work; for emergency patches we still need exceptions (post-facto notification plus review).

Internal ask: Hannah, can legal provide guidance on whether we can accept the 99.99% commitment with the following constraints?
  * maximum monthly credit cap = 20% of monthly invoice for that endpoint
  * SLA measurement excludes scheduled windows pre-notified by 48 hours and documented DR failover tests
  * we include a 6-month ramp (trial) where credits are reduced by 50% during the ramp to allow rollout validation

Jonas — can you confirm we have a runbook template and that the Regional Failover tests can be scoped to quarterly smoke tests with defined SLOs?

Peter & procurement team — if this approach sounds like a path, we'll push a clean Order Form with tracked changes and a redline compare to get legal redlines working in parallel.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lang <peter.lang@auriga.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jul 2028 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: SLA availability quantum & maintenance notification protocol - legal position & proposed compromise

Peter / team —

We reviewed Auriga's annotated redlines and Marissa's suggested trade-offs. Legal position and proposed compromise below (for contract language updates):

1) Availability commitment: We can accept a 99.99% monthly uptime commitment for the designated "Primary Inference Endpoint" provided all of the following are incorporated:
   - A clear definition of the Primary Inference Endpoint by URL and routing policy in the Order Form.
   - A maximum monthly credit cap at 20% of charges for that endpoint (cap applies to all combined credits).
   - A 6-month operational ramp where credits are reduced to 50% for the first 6 months after go-live to allow tuning and initial failover exercises.

2) Measurement & credits: Language will reflect a per-minute calculation but with a monthly bucket (so credits are calculated per-minute but applied as aggregated monthly credit per the matrix). This addresses Auriga's visibility and our operational stability concerns.

3) Maintenance & notifications: We can shorten planned maintenance notice to 48 hours for scheduled maintenance that affects the Primary Endpoint. Emergency patches remain an exclusion where we will provide post-event reports within 24 hours and a remediation plan within 72 hours.

4) Regional failover runbook & testing: Accept to include a runbook appendix and quarterly smoke-test cadence. Tests must be scheduled with at least one week's notice and have pass/fail criteria; failed tests do not trigger credits but will require a remediation plan.

Next steps:
- We'll prepare a clean Order Form with tracked changes (Order Form v3) reflecting the above and circulate for signature.
- Marissa: if Auriga confirms acceptance of the 20% cap and ramp terms, we can fold the language into v3 and send to DocuSign.

Attachments: Order_Form_v3_draft.pdf (will circulate within 24 hours)

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (650) 555-0199
